nodes.characterization_summary: Significant morphological changes observed: NFOOH evolves from disordered nanosheets to larger defined nanosheets; Ce0.33-NFOOH from underdeveloped nanosheets to stacked nanogranular structure indicative of Fe dissolution and redeposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images, Figures 2(a1) and 2(a2) and 2(b1) and 2(b2), reveal significant morphological changes in NFOOH and Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH during reconstruction. The NFOOH evolves from disordered nanosheets to larger, more defined nanosheets, while Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH transitions from an underdeveloped nanosheet structure to a stacked nanogranular configuration, indicative of Fe dissolution and redeposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: NFOOH_before shows γ-FeOOH peaks at 14.1° (020), 27.1° (120) and α-FeOOH broadening 16.5°-27°; after reconstruction γ-FeOOH disappears, α-FeOOH broadening more pronounced indicating phase transformation. Ce0.33-NFOOH_before shows only α-FeOOH broadening; after shows γ-FeOOH broadening 10°-16° and (020) peak, plus CeO2 peaks at 28.5° (111), 47.5° (220).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis further supports these observations. For NFOOH [Fig. 2(e)], diffraction peaks at 14.1° and 27.1° correspond to the (020) and (120) lattice planes of γ-FeOOH (PDF#00-008-0098), while the broadening peak between 16.5° and 27° ... can be attributed to overlapping reflections from the (020), (110), and (120) planes of α-FeOOH ... After reconstruction, the diffraction peaks corresponding to γ-FeOOH disappear, and broadening associated with α-FeOOH becomes more pronounced.

nodes.characterization_summary: NFOOH_after confirms low crystallinity α-FeOOH with short-range (130) lattice fringes and dilated 3.77 Å spacing from overlapping (020)/(110)/(120) planes. Ce0.33-NFOOH_after confirms γ-FeOOH phase with distinctive curved (020) lattice fringes at dilated spacing 2.633 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images of NFOOH_{(after)} [Fig. 2(c1)] further confirm the presence of low crystallinity α-FeOOH, with short-range lattice fringes corresponding to the (130) crystal planes, as well as dilated spacings (3.77 Å) associated with the broadening and overlapping of (020), (110), and (120) planes observed in XRD ... HRTEM image of Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH_{(after)} [Fig. 2(d1)] further confirms the γ-FeOOH phase, showing the distinctive and curved lattice fringes of the (020) crystal plane with dilated spacing 2.633 Å, consistent with XRD observations.

nodes.characterization_summary: NFOOH shows Ni-O vibrations at 472 cm^{-1} (E_g bending δ(Ni-O)), 551 cm^{-1} (A_{1g} stretching ν(Ni-O)); weak α-FeOOH Fe^{3+}-O at 680 cm^{-1} becomes more pronounced after reconstruction. Ce0.33-NFOOH_before: α-FeOOH peaks at 300, 680 cm^{-1} plus Ni-O peaks; after: α-FeOOH peaks vanish, replaced by asymmetric CeO2 peak at 470 cm^{-1} and γ-FeOOH characteristic peak at 250 cm^{-1}.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For NFOOH [Fig. S3(a)], the Raman spectra before and after reconstruction show two peaks at 472 and 551 cm^{-1}, corresponding to the E_g bending [δ(Ni-O)] and A_{1g} stretching [ν(Ni-O)] vibrations of Ni–O bond ... A weak peak at 680 cm^{-1}, attributed to the Fe^{3+}-O stretching vibration [ν(Fe^{3+}-O)] in α-FeOOH, becomes more pronounced after reconstruction ... In contrast, the Raman spectra of Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH [Fig. S3(b)] differ significantly before and after reconstruction ... After reconstruction, these peaks vanish, replaced by an asymmetric CeO_2 peak at 470 cm^{-1} and a characteristic peak of γ-FeOOH at 250 cm^{-1}.

nodes.characterization_summary: NFOOH Fe 2p: Fe(II) 2p_{3/2} 711.0 eV, Fe(III) 2p_{3/2} 713.5 eV unchanged after reconstruction; Fe/Ni atomic ratio decreases from 1.694 to 0.425 indicating Fe loss. Ce0.33-NFOOH Fe 2p: Fe(II) 711.0 eV, Fe(III) 2p_{3/2} shifts 712.5→712.9 eV (α→γ-FeOOH); Fe/Ni increases 0.575→0.719. Ce 3d shows Ce(III)→Ce(IV) transition (doublet→triplet splitting). Reconstructed Ce0.33-NFOOH shows significantly stronger K 2p signal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution (HR) XPS spectra of Fe 2p for pristine NFOOH [Fig. 4(a), left] reveal two peaks at 711.0 and 713.5 eV, corresponding to the Fe(II) 2p_{3/2} and Fe(III) 2p_{3/2} spin–orbit characteristic peaks, respectively ... The Fe/Ni atomic ratio ... reveals a significant decrease from 1.694 to 0.425 after reconstruction ... for Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH, the Fe(III) 2p_{3/2} spin–orbit peak shifts from 712.5 to 712.9 eV after reconstruction ... The HRXPS spectra of Ce 3d in Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH [Fig. 4(c)] show a transition from doublet to triplet splitting in the Ce 3d_{3/2} characteristic peaks after reconstruction, indicative of the oxidation of Ce(III) to Ce(IV).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings of reconstructed Ce0.33-NFOOH show substantial spatial overlap between K and Fe, but misalignment between K and Ce, indicating K^+ predominantly intercalated into γ-FeOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Overlaying the K elemental map with those of Ce and Fe reveals a significant spatial misalignment between K and Ce, whereas substantial overlap is observed between K and Fe. These findings indicate that K^+ is predominantly intercalated into the γ-FeOOH phase of reconstructed Ce_{0.33}-NFOOH.
